'''Ana Caraiani''' (born 1984)<ref name="satter">{{cite press release |author=<!-- not stated --> |date= October 22, 2024 |title=Caraiani to Receive 2025 AMS Satter Prize |url=https://www.ams.org/news?news_id=7377 |location= |publisher= |agency= |access-date=February 5, 2026}}</ref> is a [[Romanians|Romanian]] mathematician, who is a [[Royal Society University Research Fellowship|Royal Society University Research Fellow]] and Professor at [[Imperial College London]]. Her research interests include [[algebraic number theory]] and the [[Langlands program]].

==Education==
She was born in [[Bucharest]]<ref>{{citation|url=https://thebestschools.org/features/50-top-women-in-stem/|title=50 Top Women in STEM|website=thebestschools.org|date=October 29, 2020|access-date=January 6, 2021|archive-date=January 9, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210109165345/https://thebestschools.org/features/50-top-women-in-stem/|url-status=dead}}</ref> and studied at [[Mihai Viteazul National College (Bucharest)|Mihai Viteazul High School]].<ref name="curier"/> In 2001, Caraiani became the first Romanian female competitor in 25 years at the [[International Mathematical Olympiad]], where she won a silver medal. In the following two years, she won two gold medals.<ref name="cv"/><ref name="rimer">{{citation |first=Sara|last= Rimer |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2008/10/10/education/10math.html |title=Math Skills Suffer in U.S., Study Finds |newspaper=[[The New York Times]] |date=October 10, 2008 |access-date=January 6, 2021}}</ref><ref name="curier">{{citation|title=Ana Caraiani – de la "Mihai Viteazul" – medalie de aur si la Olimpiada de Matematica de la Tokyo|language=Romanian|newspaper=[[Curierul Național]]|date=July 21, 2003|url=http://www.curierulnational.ro/Eveniment/2003-07-21/Ana+Caraiani+-+de+la+%E2%80%9EMihai+Viteazul%E2%80%9C+-+medalie+de+aur+si+la+Olimpiada+de+Matematica+de+la+Tokyo|access-date=December 30, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141231020358/http://www.curierulnational.ro/Eveniment/2003-07-21/Ana+Caraiani+-+de+la+%E2%80%9EMihai+Viteazul%E2%80%9C+-+medalie+de+aur+si+la+Olimpiada+de+Matematica+de+la+Tokyo|archive-date=December 31, 2014|url-status=dead}}.</ref>

After graduating high school in 2003, she pursued her studies in the United States.<ref>{{citation|url=https://jurnalul.ro/special-jurnalul/ana-matematica-pura-68131.html|title=Ana: matematica pură|language=ro|newspaper=[[Jurnalul Național]]|date=May 31, 2004|access-date=January 6, 2021}}</ref> As an undergraduate student at [[Princeton University]], Caraiani was a two-time [[Putnam Fellow]] (the only female competitor at the [[William Lowell Putnam Mathematical Competition]] to win more than once) and [[Elizabeth Lowell Putnam]] Award winner.<ref name="cv"/><ref name="schafer"/><ref>{{citation|title=Caraiani wins prestigious Putnam prize at math competition|newspaper=[[Daily Princetonian]]|first=Ellen|last=Young|date=April 14, 2004|url=http://dailyprincetonian.com/news/2004/04/caraiani-wins-prestigious-putnam-prize-at-math-competition/|access-date=December 30, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141231014947/http://dailyprincetonian.com/news/2004/04/caraiani-wins-prestigious-putnam-prize-at-math-competition/|archive-date=December 31, 2014|url-status=dead}}.</ref> Caraiani graduated ''[[summa cum laude]]'' from Princeton in 2007, with an undergraduate thesis on [[Galois module|Galois representations]] supervised by [[Andrew Wiles]].<ref name="cv"/>

Caraiani did her graduate studies at [[Harvard University]] under the supervision of Wiles' student [[Richard Taylor (mathematician)|Richard Taylor]], earning her Ph.D. in 2012 with a dissertation concerning local-global compatibility in the [[Langlands program|Langlands correspondence]].<ref name="cv"/><ref>{{mathgenealogy|id=179644}}.</ref>

==Career==
After spending a year as an L.E. Dickson Instructor at the [[University of Chicago]], she returned to Princeton and the [[Institute for Advanced Study]] as a Veblen Instructor and NSF Postdoctoral Fellow.<ref name="cv"/> In 2016, she moved to the [[Hausdorff Center for Mathematics]] as a Bonn Junior Fellow.<ref name="cv"/> She moved to [[Imperial College London]] in 2017 as a Royal Society University Research Fellow and Senior Lecturer.<ref name="cv">{{citation |url=http://wwwf.imperial.ac.uk/~acaraian/cv.pdf |title=Ana Caraiani |website=Ana Caraiani |accessdate=March 21, 2021}}</ref> In 2019, she became a Royal Society University Research Fellow and Reader at Imperial College London.<ref name="cv"/> As of 2021, Caraiani is a full professor at Imperial College London.<ref>{{citation |url=https://www.imperial.ac.uk/people/a.caraiani |title=Home – Professor Ana Caraiani |website=[[Imperial College London]] |accessdate=September 10, 2021}}</ref> She was also Hausdorff Chair at [[University of Bonn]] in 2022-2023. <ref>{{citation |url=https://www.ma.imperial.ac.uk/~acaraian/cv.pdf |title=Home – Professor Ana Caraiani CV|website=[[Imperial College London]] |accessdate=August 19, 2025}}</ref>

==Recognition==
In 2007, the [[Association for Women in Mathematics]] awarded Caraiani their [[Alice T. Schafer Prize]].<ref name="cv"/><ref name="schafer">[http://www.awm-math.org/schaferprize/2007.html Seventeenth Annual Alice T. Schafer Prize], [[Association for Women in Mathematics]], retrieved December 30, 2014.</ref> In 2018, she was one of the winners of the [[Whitehead Prize]] of the [[London Mathematical Society]].<ref>{{citation|url=https://www.ams.org/journals/notices/201809/rnoti-p1118.pdf|journal=[[Notices of the American Mathematical Society]]|volume=65|issue=9|date=October 2018|page=1122|department=Mathematics People|title=Prizes of the London Mathematical Society}}</ref>

She was elected as a [[Fellow of the American Mathematical Society]] in the 2020 Class, for "contributions to arithmetic geometry and number theory, in particular the <math>p</math>-adic Langlands program".<ref>{{citation|url=https://www.ams.org/profession/ams-fellows/new-fellows|title=2020 Class of the Fellows of the AMS|publisher=[[American Mathematical Society]]|access-date=November 3, 2019}}</ref> She is one of the 2020 winners of the [[EMS Prize]].<ref>{{citation|url=https://euro-math-soc.eu/news/20/05/8/prize-winners-announced|title=Prize Winners Announced|publisher=[[European Mathematical Society]]|date=May 8, 2020}}</ref> In September 2022 she was awarded the 2023 [[Breakthrough Prize in Mathematics|New Horizons in Mathematics Prize]].<ref>{{citation|url=https://breakthroughprize.org/News/73|title=Winners of the 2023 Breakthrough Prizes in Life Sciences, Mathematics and Fundamental Physics Announced| website=breakthroughprize.org| publisher=[[Breakthrough Prize]]|date=September 22, 2022|access-date=December 26, 2022}}</ref> She was elected to the [[Academia Europaea]] in 2024.<ref>{{citation|url=https://www.ae-info.org/ae/Member/Caraiani_Ana|title=Ana Caraiani|work=Members|publisher=Academia Europaea|access-date=2024-11-09}}</ref> In 2025 she was awarded the [[Ruth Lyttle Satter Prize in Mathematics]].<ref name="satter"/>
